sub: Entity-Relationship modelling
q: A property that describes various characteristics of entity
exp: An attribute is the named property that describes a characteristic of an entity, such as name or age of a Student. "Column" is the physical relational-table word for the same idea and is the standard trap here; the ER-model vocabulary the question uses is "attribute".

q: Tree structures are used to store data in this model
exp: The hierarchical model stores records as a tree in which every child segment has exactly one parent. The network model is the usual distractor: it also uses pointers, but its structure is a graph, so a record may have several parents.

sub: SQL and basic query statements
q: This clause specifies the query result should be sorted in ascending or descending order based on the values of one or more columns
exp: ORDER BY sorts the result set ascending (default) or descending on one or more listed columns. GROUP BY only collapses rows into groups and HAVING only filters those groups; neither imposes any ordering.

sub: Database design, functional dependencies and normal forms
q: Fifth Normal form is concerned with
exp: Fifth normal form, also called project-join normal form, removes join dependencies that are not implied by the candidate keys. Multivalued dependency is the trap: that is what 4NF addresses, while functional dependency belongs to 2NF/3NF/BCNF.

sub: Concurrency control, locking and time stamping
q: When two or more users are waiting for data locked by each other, such situations are known to be
exp: A circular wait in which each transaction holds a lock the other needs is the textbook definition of deadlock. The DBMS must break it by detection-and-rollback of a victim, or prevent it by a scheme such as wait-die or wound-wait.

sub: Database design, functional dependencies and normal forms
q: Generating a set of relation schemas that allows storing information without unnecessary redundancy, is goal of
exp: Normalization is exactly the process of decomposing relation schemas so that data is stored without unnecessary redundancy and without insert, update or delete anomalies. Assertions and integrity constraints police the data; they do not design the schemas.

sub: Database design, functional dependencies and normal forms
q: If both the functional dependencies : X→Y and Y→X hold for two attributes X and Y then the relationship between X and Y is
exp: X to Y means each X value has exactly one Y value, and Y to X means each Y value has exactly one X value; together that makes the mapping one-to-one. A single-sided dependency X to Y alone would only give M:1.

q: If α → β holds then so does
exp: This is Armstrong's augmentation axiom: if alpha determines beta, then adding the same attribute set gamma to both sides preserves the dependency, so gamma-alpha determines gamma-beta. Option (b) does not follow, because nothing guarantees that alpha determines gamma, so (c) fails with it.

sub: Query processing and optimisation
q: As per equivalence rules for query transformation, selection operation distributes over
exp: The standard equivalence rule for query transformation states that selection distributes over all three set operations: union, intersection and set difference. For set difference the weaker form also holds (the selection need only be applied to the first relation), but applying it to both operands remains valid.

sub: Database design, functional dependencies and normal forms
q: In 2NF
exp: Second normal form is 1NF plus the requirement that no non-prime attribute is dependent on only part of a candidate key, i.e. no partial functional dependencies remain. Multivalued dependencies are the concern of 4NF, so the MVD options are out of scope.

sub: Entity-Relationship modelling
q: Total participation in ER Diagram is represented by
exp: In Chen notation total participation, meaning every entity in the set must take part in the relationship, is drawn as a double line joining the entity set to the relationship set. A single line denotes partial participation.

sub: Concurrency control, locking and time stamping
q:
Which of the following concurrency control protocols ensure both conflict serializability and freedom from deadlock?
I. Time-stamp ordering
II. 2-phase locking
exp: Timestamp ordering never makes a transaction wait for another's lock: a conflicting operation is rejected and the transaction is rolled back and restarted, so it is conflict serializable and inherently deadlock-free. Basic two-phase locking guarantees conflict serializability but transactions block on locks and can deadlock. Option (d) is misprinted as "Neither I nor III", but it is not the answer either way.
note: Only the questions matching the 2026 syllabus were imported from this paper (36 of 100). Printed option (d) reads 'Neither I nor III' though the stem lists only I and II; transcribed as printed.

sub: Transaction processing, schedules and recoverability
q: Which of the following is false regarding ACID properties in DBMS?

opts.B: It decrease complexity of the system

exp: The false statement is that ACID decreases system complexity: enforcing atomicity, consistency, isolation and durability requires logging, locking and recovery machinery, which increases complexity. The other three are true, including the performance overhead that ACID guarantees impose.

sub: Database design, functional dependencies and normal forms
q: While designing a database , the one guideline to be followed is

opts.B: A database design may be ambiguous
opts.C: Unrelated data should be in the same table so that updating the data will be easy
opts.D: Data entity should not have attributes

exp: A core database design guideline is to avoid or minimise redundancy, since duplicated data is what produces update, insert and delete anomalies. The other options invert good practice: a design must be unambiguous, unrelated data belongs in separate tables, and an entity without attributes carries no information.

sub: Query processing and optimisation
q: The process of finding a good strategy for processing a query is called
exp: Query optimization is the step that selects a good evaluation plan from the many equivalent ones for a query. Query processing is the whole pipeline of parsing, optimization and evaluation, and query cost is the metric the optimizer uses, not the process itself.

sub: Data models and the relational model: keys, tuples, domains and relational algebra
q: A second form of relational calculus, is known as
exp: Domain relational calculus is presented as the second form of relational calculus, after tuple relational calculus; its variables range over the domains of individual attributes rather than over whole tuples. It has the same expressive power as tuple calculus and relational algebra when restricted to safe expressions.

sub: Database system concepts, architecture, interfaces and data independence
q: The two files that are used during operation of the DBMS.
exp: The data dictionary holds the metadata the DBMS consults on every access, and the transaction log records changes for recovery, so these are the two files the DBMS itself uses during operation. Query languages, utilities and DML are tools or interfaces rather than files.

q: In tuple relational calculus P1 AND P2 is equivalent to
exp: By De Morgan's law, P1 AND P2 is the negation of (NOT P1 OR NOT P2), which is option (b) exactly. Options (c) and (d) negate only one of the two predicates before the outer negation, so they reduce to (NOT P1 AND P2) and (P1 AND NOT P2) respectively; that asymmetry is how they are printed on the paper and it is what makes them wrong.

sub: Web architecture, client-server communication, HTTP/HTTPS, DNS and hosting
q: This is responsible for the management of Internet domain names and addresses
exp: ICANN (Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers) coordinates the global domain name system and IP address allocation. NIC here is a network interface card (or a national registry), ISOC is the policy/education body behind the IETF, and the printed 'IEFE' is a misspelling of IETF, which writes protocol standards rather than managing names.

sub: SQL and basic query statements
q: This operator is used to compare a value to a list of literals values that have been specified.
exp: The IN operator tests whether a value matches any member of an explicitly listed set of literals, e.g. WHERE dept IN ('CS','EE','ME'). BETWEEN compares against a continuous range rather than a list, LIKE does pattern matching on strings, and SQL has no COMPARE operator.

sub: Data models and the relational model: keys, tuples, domains and relational algebra
q: A list consists of last names, first names, addresses and pin codes. If all people in the list have the same last name and same pin code a useful key would be

opts.C: the compound key last name and pin code
opts.D: the compound key first name and last name

exp: A key must discriminate between rows, so any attribute that is identical for everyone (last name, pin code) carries zero distinguishing power, which also kills the last-name+pin-code compound. Only the compound including the first name varies across the list, so it is the only workable key of the four, even though strictly it distinguishes on the first name alone.

sub: Entity-Relationship modelling
q: Specialization ,in an E-R diagram, is represented by a
exp: In the arrow-based ER notation, specialization/generalization is drawn as a hollow (open) triangular arrow-head on the line running from the subclass up to the superclass, distinguishing it from ordinary relationship lines. Note that Silberschatz's main notation instead uses an ISA triangle, so this question is testing the alternative arrow convention; dashed and solid arrow-heads carry other meanings (weak/derived links and cardinality direction).

sub: Database system concepts, architecture, interfaces and data independence
q: Large collection of files are called
exp: The classic data hierarchy runs bit to character to field to record to file to database, so a large collection of related files is a database. Records and fields sit below the file level, and sectors are a physical disk-storage unit, not a logical grouping of files.

sub: Data models and the relational model: keys, tuples, domains and relational algebra
q: This is not a logical database structure
exp: The recognised logical database structures are relational, hierarchical (tree) and network; 'chain' is not one of them, it merely names a pointer-linking technique used inside file organisations. Tree is simply the usual name for the hierarchical model, so it does not qualify as the odd one out.

sub: Data models and the relational model: keys, tuples, domains and relational algebra
q: For enforcing data integrity, it is a preferred method
exp: Declarative constraints (PRIMARY KEY, FOREIGN KEY, UNIQUE, CHECK, NOT NULL) are the preferred integrity mechanism because the DBMS enforces them automatically for every access path and can optimise around them. Triggers and stored procedures can enforce the same rules only procedurally, at higher cost and with more room for bugs, and cursors have nothing to do with integrity.

sub: Database system concepts, architecture, interfaces and data independence
q: It defines overall design of the database
exp: The schema is the overall design of the database, the structure that stays fixed while the instance (the stored data) changes. DDL is only the language used to write the schema down, which is the trap here: the artefact defining the design is the schema, not the language that expresses it.

sub: Entity-Relationship modelling
q: Mapping cardinalities are useful in describing
exp: Mapping cardinality states how many entities of one set can associate with entities of another (1:1, 1:M, M:1, M:M), which is well defined only when exactly two entity sets are involved. Standard texts say plainly that mapping cardinalities are most useful in describing binary relationship sets; for relationships of higher degree the notion becomes ambiguous.

sub: Database system concepts, architecture, interfaces and data independence
q: It refers to the correctness and completeness of the data in a database
exp: Data integrity is the property that stored data is accurate, complete and consistent over its lifetime. Data security is about protecting data from unauthorised access, data independence about insulating applications from schema changes, and a constraint is one of the tools used to enforce integrity rather than the property itself.
note: Only the questions matching the 2026 syllabus were imported from this paper (36 of 100).

sub: Transaction processing, schedules and recoverability
q: Efficient implementation of a recovery scheme requires that the number of writes to be ________.
exp: Log-based recovery forces log records and data blocks out to stable storage, and every such output is an expensive disk write, so an efficient scheme keeps the number of writes to a minimum (this is exactly why checkpointing and deferred/immediate update schemes try to batch or postpone output). 'Maximum' would defeat the purpose, and dependent/independent describe no recognised efficiency criterion here.

sub: Entity-Relationship modelling
q: An relationship among students and courses is
exp: One student enrols in many courses and one course is taken by many students, so student-course enrolment is the textbook many-to-many relationship, which in a relational schema is resolved by an extra junction table holding the pair of keys.

sub: Database system concepts, architecture, interfaces and data independence
q: The metadata is created by
exp: Metadata is the description of the database structure itself, and it is produced when the DDL interpreter parses CREATE/ALTER statements and records the resulting definitions in the data dictionary. The DML compiler and its pre-processor only translate data-manipulation statements against a schema that already exists.

exp: HTTP's well-known port is 80 (HTTPS uses 443). Port 21 is FTP's control connection and 43 is WHOIS, both common distractors in this style of question.

q: Algebraic operation that outputs specified attributes from all rows of the input relation, is said to be
exp: Projection picks columns: it keeps the listed attributes from every tuple of the relation and discards the rest. Selection is the mirror-image operation that keeps whole rows satisfying a predicate, which is the usual confusion in this pair.

sub: Concurrency control, locking and time stamping
q: If a transaction T has obtained an exclusive lock on item Q, then T can

opts.D: write Q but not read Q

exp: An exclusive (X) lock grants full access, so the holder may both read and write the item, while all other transactions are locked out entirely. The trap is (d): exclusive mode does not forbid reading, it is the shared (S) lock that permits reading only.

sub: Database design, functional dependencies and normal forms
q: If the closure of an attribute set is the entire relation, then the attribute set is a
exp: If the attribute closure under the given FDs yields every attribute of the relation, the set functionally determines the whole tuple, which is precisely the definition of a super key. It is only a candidate key if it is additionally minimal, i.e. no proper subset has the same full closure, so 'candidate key' is the classic over-claim here.

sub: Entity-Relationship modelling
q: It is an abstraction through which relationships are treated as higher level entities
exp: Aggregation is the ER abstraction that treats an entire relationship set as though it were a single higher-level entity, so it can itself participate in another relationship (e.g. a works-on relationship linked to a manages relationship). Generalization and specialization abstract over entity sets, not relationships.
